title: Adab with children
hook: a kiss for a grandson, a man who never kissed his own, and one short sentence about mercy

segments.voice: Yesterday, adab with neighbors, and your line: safe beside you. Did one neighbor get a knock or a word? Today, the smallest people in the house. Day one thousand three hundred three.

A grandfather bends down and kisses a small boy. Nothing unusual, except who's watching. In Sahih al-Bukhari, in paraphrase, the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, kissed his grandson al-Hasan, while a man named al-Aqra' ibn Habis sat nearby. Al-Aqra' said: I have ten children, and I have never kissed a single one of them. The Prophet looked at him. And what he said next is today's lesson, short enough to fit on a fridge.
screen: `A KISS FOR AL-HASAN.` → `TEN CHILDREN, NEVER KISSED.` → `THE PROPHET LOOKED AT HIM.`

segments.voice: Here is his answer, in paraphrase from Bukhari: whoever does not show mercy is not shown mercy. In Arabic it's short: man la yarham la yurham. One verb, turned from giving mercy to receiving it. Give it, and it is given to you. Hold it back, and it is held back. He didn't argue about customs or toughness. He simply tied the kiss to mercy, and mercy to the One who shows mercy. Bukhari keeps a second report like it. A desert Arab came and said, in paraphrase: you kiss children? We don't kiss them. And the Prophet answered: what can I do for you, if Allah has taken mercy from your heart? Notice where he locates the problem. Not in the hands. In the heart. Then a scene that turns adab with children into something you can see. Also in Bukhari, in paraphrase: the Prophet prayed carrying his granddaughter Umamah. When he went down into prostration, he set her down. When he stood, he picked her up again. The prayer itself, and a small child carried through it. Nobody sent her out of the room. So the adab here isn't a list of rules for children. It's the adults' manners toward them: tenderness shown openly, affection that doesn't wait for a child to earn it, room for them even in the middle of worship. And the line holds both ways. The mercy you give a small person is tied, in this hadith, to the mercy you hope to receive.
screen: `WHOEVER SHOWS NO MERCY IS SHOWN NONE.` · `NOT IN THE HANDS. IN THE HEART.` · `UMAMAH CARRIED THROUGH PRAYER.` · `MERCY GIVEN, MERCY RECEIVED.`

segments.voice: Settle, and breathe slowly. Bring to mind a child in your life: your own, a niece or nephew, a grandchild, a neighbor's kid, a student. See their face. Notice how they ask for attention, and how often they get it. If there's a child near you today, the practice is simple: a hug, or a kiss on the head, offered openly, with nothing asked back. If there isn't, remember a time an adult was gentle with you when you were small, and hold that memory for a moment. If you pray, you can ask mercy for that child. The bell holds the time.
Adab with children. The manners of the grown-ups toward the small ones: open tenderness, room for them even in prayer, and mercy given so mercy is received. Today's word.
Your line: mercy for mercy. Today, give one child your full attention for a minute, or a hug, with nothing asked back. Tomorrow, adab with creation. Day one thousand three hundred three.

howItsDone: The hadith collections show the Prophet kissing his grandson and carrying his granddaughter Umamah in prayer as open tenderness toward children, summed up in the hadith that whoever does not show mercy is not shown mercy.

notes: 'Ten children' is in the text of Bukhari 5997; confirm.
Confirm transliteration of man la yarham la yurham.
